note: Phase I refused every EXTERNAL_WORLD effect by class. That refusal was doing two jobs: keeping irreversible acts behind an owner, and keeping ordinary coordination behind one too. This separates them. An effect inside a declared scope below, carrying a receipt, is admitted without a further owner act. Everything else is refused by name. The blanket refusal is gone; the boundary is not.

authorized_by.basis: Bdo, 2026-08-23 interactive session: unblock it all; 2026-08-25 direction: completed merged feature branches retire automatically; 2026-08-26 direction: refine every issue, updating metadata, comments and bodies

compensation_model: Forward compensation only. An external effect is never claimed to be rolled back. A counteraction records the original occurrence, the remedy attempted, what remains changed or consumed, and the evidence for both. A receipt that claims world rollback is a defect against this contract.
receipt_note: Every attempt leaves a receipt whether it succeeded, failed, or was refused. An effect with no receipt is indistinguishable from an effect that never happened, which is the state this contract exists to prevent.

coordination.issue_metadata.reversible_by: applying the inverse verb; the original value is recorded in the receipt before the write, and a body is restored by writing the recorded prior body back
coordination.issue_metadata.note: The ordinary board work: labels, project fields, open/closed state, comments, and the issue body. The body carried the authoritative metadata block while every label was only its projection, so until decision 0067 a scope existed for writing the projection and none for writing the source: an agent could relabel a ticket to match a block it was refused permission to correct. A body write that would produce a block the schema refuses is itself refused, so this verb cannot manufacture a defective ticket.

preconditions.statement: the body being written parses as soveraeign-ticket/v1 and validates against contracts/issue-metadata.schema.json
the body as it stood before the write is recorded in the receipt

coordination.branch_write.reversible_by: deleting the branch or closing the pull request; no published history is rewritten
coordination.branch_write.note: Publishing work for review. Fast-forward only.

coordination.branch_retirement.target: github.com/bdf1992/Soveraeign same-repository pull-request head refs after merge

preconditions.statement: GitHub currently reports the named pull request merged
the pull request head ref exactly equals the branch being deleted
the pull request head SHA exactly equals the merge event head SHA
the pull request head repository is bdf1992/Soveraeign
the pull request base ref exactly equals the merge event base ref
the repository default branch is not the branch being deleted
the live branch ref still points exactly at the merged pull request head SHA
no open pull request currently uses the head branch as its base

coordination.branch_retirement.reversible_by: recreating the ref at the recorded merged head SHA; merged commits and the pull-request record remain addressable
coordination.branch_retirement.note: Retires completed execution inventory only. Behindness, age, silence, containment guesses, and caller assertions do not authorize deletion. A reused or advanced ref, protected default branch, or open stacked child makes retirement refuse.

refused_verbs.delete_branch_shared: Removes a ref other work may depend on. DESTRUCTIVE_ADMIN. A branch with an open pull request based on it is shared and cannot use coordination.branch_retirement.
refused_verbs.change_branch_protection: Changes who may write, which is an authority change, not coordination.
refused_verbs.change_repository_settings: Changes the boundary rather than acting inside it.
refused_verbs.merge_pull_request: Merging is settlement, and settlement belongs to the owning seat rather than to the adapter.
refused_verbs.act_outside_this_repository: Every scope above names one repository. Another target needs its own scope.

refusal_codes.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_UNAUTHORIZED: The request declares EXTERNAL_WORLD and names no scope in this contract.
refusal_codes.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_OUT_OF_SCOPE: The named scope does not carry the requested verb or target.
refusal_codes.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_VERB_REFUSED: The verb is named in refused_verbs.
refusal_codes.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_WITHOUT_RECEIPT: The request carries no receipt address, so the attempt would leave no record.
refusal_codes.EXTERNAL_EFFECT_PRECONDITION_UNMET: The named scope carries the verb and the request does not discharge every precondition that verb carries: one is unnamed, its evidence is empty, or the request discharges a precondition the verb does not carry.

precondition_model: A precondition binds the verbs it names, not the whole scope: a body write answers the body preconditions and a label write is never asked for them. Every precondition declared here is decided by reading the live remote, which the authorization boundary cannot do, so the boundary and the proof hold one half each. The boundary refuses EXTERNAL_EFFECT_PRECONDITION_UNMET unless the request discharges, by id, every precondition its verb carries and names the evidence that discharged it. The discharged_by proof is what performs the read and refuses there. Neither half is a boundary alone: a proof the boundary does not demand is skipped by any caller that does not run it, and an attestation with no proof behind it is a caller vouching for itself. Declaring a precondition and reading it nowhere is the third and worst state, because the contract then reads as a guard that is not one. What is true as of this writing, and is not yet the join this paragraph describes: the two halves exist and are not wired to each other. adapters/github/apply.py is the only module permitted to write to GitHub, and it calls the discharged_by proofs directly through its own authority_basis dispatch. It builds no authorization block, carries no preconditions_discharged, and consults neither scripts/sovticket/transitions.py nor scripts/sovkernel/transitions.py. So a transition request is now refused unless it discharges, and the adapter still writes without asking. Read this section as the shape the crossing must take, not as a description of an enforced write path; wiring the adapter to the boundary is unbuilt and is named here so the gap is not mistaken for enforcement.
